findings.summary: Any authenticated user can read any invoice because ownership, tenant, and permission checks are absent.
findings.evidence: canReadInvoice returns true whenever user.authenticated and invoice are truthy.

findings.summary: The document listing returns every supplied document without restricting results to the user's tenant.
findings.evidence: listDocuments(user, documents) directly returns documents and never uses user.

findings.summary: A charge failure after reservation leaves the reservation in place, with no rollback or recovery mechanism.
findings.evidence: processOrder awaits gateway.reserve before gateway.charge but has no error handling or compensation.

findings.summary: Older status events can overwrite newer order state because event sequence ordering is not validated.
findings.evidence: applyStatus unconditionally assigns event.status and event.sequence to the order.

findings.summary: Redelivery or retry of a payment message can charge the customer multiple times.
findings.evidence: processPayment invokes provider.charge without an idempotency key or duplicate-message check.

findings.summary: Emitting individual user IDs as request attributes creates an unbounded telemetry dimension.
findings.evidence: requestAttributes assigns request.userId to the "user.id" attribute.

findings.summary: The project pins Log4j Core 2.14.1, a version affected by the Log4Shell remote-code-execution vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228).
Nested retry loops invoke the operation up to nine times, amplifying load and side effects during failures.
findings.evidence: Three outer iterations each contain three inner attempts, with no backoff or retry filtering.

findings.summary: The migration immediately drops a column, risking data loss and failures in application instances that still reference it.
findings.evidence: migration.sql contains only ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_status.
